register.name: Resilience to hurricanes in the building sector (FP133)
register.detail: Green Climate Fund · grant · approved 21 August 2020 · effective 21 July 2021 · completion estimated 21 July 2027 · 18% disbursed
register.note: Total project value $46.1 million, with $13.4 million of co-financing
register.text: A Green Climate Fund grant, managed by the Department of Environment of Antigua and Barbuda, to make critical public service and community buildings more resilient to extreme climate events, with climate information systems and support for post-disaster response. It serves the shelter standard; about 73,200 people are expected to gain resilience.
by: Department of Environment, Antigua and Barbuda

register.name: Enhanced direct access pilot for physical adaptation and community resilience (FP061)
register.detail: Green Climate Fund · grant · approved 1 March 2018 · Antigua and Barbuda, Dominica and Grenada · effective 16 July 2019 · completion estimated 16 June 2027 · 99% disbursed
register.note: Shared by three nations; total project value $22.6 million
register.text: A Green Climate Fund grant, led by the Department of Environment of Antigua and Barbuda, that pays for small grants to community organisations and revolving loans to households and businesses to make buildings more resilient to Category 5 hurricanes. It also funds drainage, irrigation and soil and water conservation, and serves the shelter and water standards.
by: Department of Environment, Antigua and Barbuda

register.name: Transforming education in Antigua and Barbuda
register.detail: Caribbean Development Bank · news release of 21 October 2026
register.note: Announced by the CDB on 21 October 2026; terms to be read at source
register.text: Financing of US$56.2 million approved by the Caribbean Development Bank to transform education in Antigua and Barbuda, announced on 21 October 2026. It serves the education standard.

register.name: Covid-19 Response Health Project
register.detail: Caribbean Development Bank · approved March 2022 · approved total $4,996,034 · part of Strengthening resilience and supporting recovery in Antigua and Barbuda
register.note: Shown as under implementation on the CDB project map
register.text: A Caribbean Development Bank project to strengthen Antigua and Barbuda’s ability to respond to pandemics and to deliver healthcare, approved in March 2022 and still under implementation. It serves the health standard.

register.name: University of the West Indies Five Islands expansion
register.detail: Saudi Fund for Development · financing agreement · release of 18 January 2023 · seven energy-efficient buildings · nearly 95,160 m²
register.note: Designed to serve 5,000 students a year
register.text: A financing agreement between the Saudi Fund for Development and the Government of Antigua and Barbuda to expand the Five Islands campus of the University of the West Indies with seven energy-efficient buildings on nearly 95,160 square metres. The campus is designed to serve 5,000 students a year, which serves the education standard.

register.name: Barbuda Energy Resilience Project
register.detail: UK Caribbean Infrastructure Fund grant, administered by the CDB · approved December 2019 · Government of Antigua and Barbuda US$6.4M · construction completion March 2027
register.note: US$3.9 million; the CDB project map shows an approved total of $2,516,535
register.text: A grant from the UK Government, administered by the Caribbean Development Bank, for a 2.9 km underground electricity network serving Codrington, hybrid solar backup for the Hanna Thomas Hospital, the Barbuda Community Centre and the Barbuda Council Building, and the reconnection of 45 households after Hurricane Irma. It serves the energy standard on Barbuda.

enterprises.heading: Already working in Antigua and Barbuda.

items.name: Granma Aki
items.text: A local agro-processing company that turns lemongrass, soursop, mango, tamarind, starfruit and other fruits into teas, sauces, jams and sweets, and now supplies major supermarkets and hotels in Antigua and Barbuda. In 2025 its founder, Novella Payne, was named a Leader of Rurality of the Americas by the Inter-American Institute for Cooperation on Agriculture.

items.name: Needful Thingz (Brusch Services)
items.text: A women-led business that operates feminine hygiene vending units in high-traffic bathrooms to provide an essential service for women, conceived as a sustainable income stream for a campaign supporting the Sunshine Home for Girls. A grant from the CIWiL Fempreneur Fund helped it scale, with new units being installed at the AUA pre-med campus.

items.name: GARD Center
items.text: The Gilbert Agricultural and Rural Development Center in Mercers Creek, a non-profit whose Business Development Unit is a one-stop training centre and business services provider for new and existing entrepreneurs. Its mission is to improve the income-generating capacities of vulnerable young women in Antigua and Barbuda.
